items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I didn’t really know Muggsy, I wish I’d known him better

ctx.x: I want to ask you a couple of things about those times. Chicago in the 30s, when you first started doing those records there, how was the depression and prohibition part of the whole atmosphere.

It’s funny, I always thought to myself that I was there in the worst time and I never really realized it. It’s probably because I wasn’t there before it. And it was hard. And of course it was hard. I took it for granted that it would be hard. Jazz was playing in The Subway, which opened at ten at night and closed at four AM, and nobody cared for them or listened to them or paid any attention. And it was like that then. And all the guys were playing in dance halls, and nobody paid any attention. You know, Muggsy…
